> 達生之情者，不務生之所無以為；達命之情者，不務知之所無奈何。

One who understands the actual state of life does not pursue what life has no use for. One who understands the actual state of fate does not pursue what knowing cannot reach.

The chapter is commonly filed under "health." The first word rules that out.

## 達 is not "cultivate"

達: to reach through, to understand something as it is.

達生 is not 養生. It is understanding the actual condition of a life — which parts are inside the allotment and which are not.

## 無以為 is not "helpless"

生之所無以為 — 無以為 means "there is no place where it is used for anything." Not "cannot be done." Not "no way." It is: no use.

That is a sharper instrument than "don't overdo it." It removes a whole category of effort: work that has no location in the thing itself, only in someone's idea of the thing.

## 神全: the spirit unharmed

神全 — spirit complete, unbroken.

What breaks it is not suffering. It is fear, gain and loss, liking and disliking — each of which cuts a piece off and holds it. The chapter's practice is therefore not accumulation. It is not being cut.

## 遻物而不慴

遻: to meet, to encounter. 慴: to be frightened.

Meet things without being frightened — which is the operating definition of 神全 in daily use.

## 開天之天，不開人之天

Open the heaven in you; do not open the human in you. 開天者德生，開人者賊生.

The human here is not "humanity." It is the made layer: division, calculation, the apparatus of 機心. Develop that and 賊 arises — not wickedness, but theft: something taken from you.

This is the chapter's line in the sand, and it is drawn in the same place as 天地's 機心 and 刻意's 刻意.

## 殙: betting with gold

殙: muddled, darkened. 以黃金注者殙 — the one who bets with gold goes dark.

The same skill, the same target, and one change of stake, and the hand fails. Which is the empirical proof of 神全: it is not a skill, because skills do not degrade when the stake rises.

## 以天合天

The first 天: your own nature, undisturbed. The second 天: the object's own nature, as it is.

Join the two. 梓慶's three, five, seven days of fasting are the method — stripping away each layer of "what I care about" until the bell can be made from the wood's own grain rather than from his ambition about it.

## 忘適之適

The highest ease is 忘適之適 — ease that has forgotten it is at ease.

Note that this is the only real test of the whole chapter. The moment you know you are calm, the measurement has started again, and 神 is being cut a little.

## The test

Take one effort you are currently sustaining for your own good. Then ask the two questions from the opening: is any part of it 無以為 — no use anywhere in the actual life? And when the stake rises, does the hand go dark? The second one is not a moral question. It is a diagnostic.
